title: ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 20 under a selective policy
issue: The policy filter has an unknown (default 50%) selectivity, so with LIMIT 20 the planner walks the created_at index expecting to stop after ~40 rows. A subject whose visible rows are old forces the walk through almost the whole index.
symptom: selective subject (visible rows are the OLDEST org) is slow for naive_rls / best_practice_rls (Rows Removed by Filter close to table size, estimate 50% vs ~0.1% actual); the mid and broad subjects are fast. 'oldest' (ASC) reverses the pattern for the broad subject.

scale.meaning: rows in app.documents; scale/200 orgs, each org owns a contiguous time block (org 1 newest, last org oldest); 200 docs per org.

subjects.name: selective
subjects.note: member of only the OLDEST org (~200 docs, all at the far end of the created_at index)

subjects.name: mid
subjects.note: member of every 20th org (~5% of orgs, spread over time)

subjects.name: broad
subjects.note: member of the NEWEST 50% of orgs
